the interaction of platinum-DNA cross-links with S1 nuclease.
the kinetics of the hydrolytic degradation of platinum-DNA by S1 nulease.
understanding the mechanism of action of cisplatin, a widely used anticancer drug, on DNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
platinum-DNA complexes are digested by S-1 nuclease with the same efficiency as native DNA.
the rate of digestion of damaged DNA by S1 was reduced by a factor of two, which is consistent with the reduction of the overall rate of hydrolytic cleavage of the damaged DNA by a factor of 0.6.
the hydrolysis rate of damaged DNA is reduced by platinum-DNA cross-links.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
platinum-DNA adduction does not alter the rate of hydrolytic digestion of DNA by nuclease, but it does alter the kinetics of release of platinum adducts from damaged DNA.
platinum-DNA complexes have an inhibitory effect on the digestion of DNA by S1 endonuclease.
platinum-DNA complexes have a higher affinity for S1 nuclease than unplatinated DNA but are digested at a lower rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the kinetics of nuclease digestion is a useful method to characterize the nature of platinum-DNA damage.
S1 nuclesse digestion of DNA can be used as a tool to study the effects of platinum-DNA cross-links on the structure of the DNA backbone.
the hydrolysis kinetics of platinated double stranded DNA by nuclease is not a simple reflection of the level of DNA adducts.
